assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reframed how technology and trade reshape labour demand. The task-based view explains wage polarization, and the local-labour-market trade-shock work documents lasting adjustment costs. Both lines changed academic research and public policy debate. Strong empirical-plus-framework contribution of the kind the criteria reward.
assessment.attribution: Technology, tasks and wage inequality are most closely tied to Autor and Katz. Trade-shock evidence is tied to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. A three-person award covering both strands leaves out Dorn, and the task-model co-authors (e.g. Levy, Murnane, Acemoglu) are not on the credited list.
assessment.maturity: The skill-bias and task literature is about 20-30 years old and the China-shock work about 13 years old. Both have been replicated and extended widely, so the work is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Recent debate on how large and persistent the trade-shock effects are, and on the identification strategy.
Dorn is excluded by the three-name limit.
The recent labour-economics prize in 2023 and the 2021 prize may weigh on timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Turned intergenerational mobility into a precisely measured, place-specific quantity using population-scale administrative data. Linked to the neighbourhood-effects and exposure-effects evidence, it has had a large influence on research and policy design.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the clear intellectual leader and a co-author in nearly every key paper. Hendren and Friedman are central on neighbourhood effects and data construction. Katz is credited through the Moving to Opportunity work, and the natural-experiment tradition has many other contributors. The three-name limit makes the allocation hard.
assessment.maturity: The core papers date from 2014-2022. Replication and extension are ongoing, and the long-run effects of some interventions are still maturing. This is the least mature of the top candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees a discrete scientific discovery or a body of measurement.
Debates over causal interpretation of place effects and over some forecasting claims.
Timing: laureates this young are less typical.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The credit-cycles model showed how collateral constraints amplify and propagate small shocks into persistent fluctuations. It is a foundational mechanism in modern macro-finance and has shaped how crises and policy are analysed.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore wrote the foundational 1997 paper, which gives a clean two-person attribution. Gertler and Gilchrist are credited for the financial accelerator and empirical extensions, but Bernanke, already a laureate (2022), is central to that strand. I propose the cleaner pair.
assessment.maturity: Nearly 30 years of use, including after 2008, which is strong confirmation of relevance and robustness.
uncertainties: The 2022 prize on banks and financial crises may be judged to overlap in subject matter.
Relative weight of the Kiyotaki-Moore model versus the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist strand.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection explain exporter premia, reallocation within industries and a new channel for gains from trade. It changed both trade theory and empirical work built on firm-level data.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's 2003 model is the core contribution. Helpman's work on firm-level trade, together with Melitz and Yeaple, is a close second. Redding's contributions are more recent and quantitative. Bernard, Eaton and Jensen are important to the empirical precursors but are not credited.
assessment.maturity: More than 20 years old and the dominant framework in the field, so it is mature and well tested.
uncertainties: The empirical precursors are not credited, so the allocation could be disputed.
Overlap with the Grossman-Helpman and quantitative-trade candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand with differentiated products and endogenous prices, plus dynamic oligopoly estimation, are core tools in empirical industrial organisation. They are used in merger review and antitrust practice, which is evidence of impact beyond academia.
assessment.attribution: The BLP trio (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a natural group. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin are credited for related strands, and the list is long, so some contributors are inevitably left out.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s and has been applied for decades. It is mature and confirmed in practice.
uncertainties: Field breadth: whether the committee views this as method or as a scientific finding.
The IO empirical tradition has more contributors than the three-name limit allows.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ricardian quantitative models made it possible to measure the gains from trade and to run counterfactual policy analysis in a tractable general-equilibrium framework. This is a strong structural contribution that changed standard practice.
assessment.attribution: Kortum's 2002 model with Eaton is the foundation, and Eaton is not on the credited list. Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare are linked to the later gains-from-trade measurement work, with Arkolakis also important and not credited. Attribution is therefore incomplete, which weakens an award from this list.
assessment.maturity: Foundational work is more than 20 years old and the quantitative applications are well established.
uncertainties: Missing key contributors (Eaton, Arkolakis) make a clean laureate set difficult.
Debate over how much the measured welfare gains depend on the model's elasticity assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Developed methods for measuring adverse selection and moral hazard in insurance markets, and tied them to welfare analysis and policy design. The work demonstrates how theory and credible empirical identification combine to guide markets such as health insurance.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein and Einav are central to the modern empirical welfare approach. Salanie's contribution is more in testing theory. The foundational theory of adverse selection is already recognised by the 2001 prize, which the proposed pair builds on rather than overlaps.
assessment.maturity: Core work dates from the mid-2000s to the 2010s. It is reasonably established, but it may still be early relative to typical timing.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of the underlying theory (2001) might reduce perceived novelty.
Whether the committee judges the contribution as primarily empirical application.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that misallocation of inputs across firms can account for a large share of cross-country income differences, and gave a measurable framework for it. It reshaped research in macro-development and productivity.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 Hsieh-Klenow paper is the central contribution. Restuccia's work with Rogerson on policy distortions and productivity is an important parallel, but Rogerson is not credited, and this makes the allocation uncertain.
assessment.maturity: More than 15 years of follow-up work, including many applications, though the size of measured misallocation depends on measurement assumptions.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of the magnitudes to measurement error and markup assumptions.
